**North West** (born June 15, 2013) is an American rapper, singer, record producer,[\[4\]](#cite_note-:1-4) and actress. She is the eldest child of rapper [Kanye West](/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") and media personality [Kim Kardashian](/wiki/Kim_Kardashian "Kim Kardashian"). West appeared in the music video for her father's 2014 single "[Only One](/wiki/Only_One_\(Kanye_West_song\) "Only One (Kanye West song)")", and made several appearances on _[Keeping Up with the Kardashians](/wiki/Keeping_Up_with_the_Kardashians "Keeping Up with the Kardashians")_ along with her mother.

As a child actress, West made her film debut as the voice of Mini in _[Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie](/wiki/Paw_Patrol:_The_Mighty_Movie "Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie")_ in 2023.[\[5\]](#cite_note-5) In 2024, she performed "[I Just Can't Wait to Be King](/wiki/I_Just_Can%27t_Wait_to_Be_King "I Just Can't Wait to Be King")" at the [Hollywood Bowl](/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl")'s _The Lion King 30th Anniversary – A Live-to-Film Concert Event_. In February of that year, she made her recording debut on [¥$](/wiki/%C2%A5$ "¥$")'s single "[Talking / Once Again](/wiki/Talking_/_Once_Again "Talking / Once Again")",[\[6\]](#cite_note-6) which peaked at number 30 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"). She also appeared on the duo's 2024 song "[Bomb](/wiki/Vultures_2 "Vultures 2")" alongside her sister Chicago, as well as [FKA Twigs](/wiki/FKA_Twigs "FKA Twigs")'s "[Childlike Things](/wiki/Childlike_Things "Childlike Things")", where she performed in Japanese on both songs.[\[7\]](#cite_note-7)

## Life and career

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=North_West_\(musician\)&action=edit&section=1 "Edit section: Life and career")\]

### 2013–2023: Early career

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=North_West_\(musician\)&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: 2013–2023: Early career")\]

North West was born on June 15, 2013, at [Cedars-Sinai Medical Center](/wiki/Cedars-Sinai_Medical_Center "Cedars-Sinai Medical Center") in [Los Angeles](/wiki/Los_Angeles "Los Angeles"), California, to [Kanye West](/wiki/Kanye_West "Kanye West") and [Kim Kardashian](/wiki/Kim_Kardashian "Kim Kardashian").[\[8\]](#cite_note-8) At the moment, Kanye was [DJing](/wiki/DJing "DJing"), and North was born while "[Bohemian Rhapsody](/wiki/Bohemian_Rhapsody "Bohemian Rhapsody")" by [Queen](/wiki/Queen_\(band\) "Queen (band)") was played.[\[9\]](#cite_note-9) North's maternal aunts and uncle are [Kourtney Kardashian](/wiki/Kourtney_Kardashian "Kourtney Kardashian"), [Khloé Kardashian](/wiki/Khlo%C3%A9_Kardashian "Khloé Kardashian"), and [Rob Kardashian](/wiki/Rob_Kardashian "Rob Kardashian"), and her maternal half-aunts are [Kendall](/wiki/Kendall_Jenner "Kendall Jenner") and [Kylie Jenner](/wiki/Kylie_Jenner "Kylie Jenner").[\[10\]](#cite_note-ift-10) West's parents became engaged in October 2013, married in May 2014,[\[11\]](#cite_note-11) separated in February 2021 following [Kanye West's unsuccessful 2020 presidential run](/wiki/Kanye_West_2020_presidential_campaign "Kanye West 2020 presidential campaign"), and divorced in 2022,[\[12\]](#cite_note-12) by which time North had two younger brothers and a younger sister.[\[13\]](#cite_note-13) West's due date was July 12, 2013, which would have been the 64th birthday of Kanye's mother [Donda West](/wiki/Donda_West "Donda West"), and her early delivery meant she spent time in an incubator.[\[14\]](#cite_note-14)

[CBS News](/wiki/CBS_News "CBS News") described her and [Prince George of Wales](/wiki/Prince_George_of_Wales "Prince George of Wales") as the two most famous babies in the world.[\[15\]](#cite_note-Lusk-2014-15) Kim told _[GQ](/wiki/GQ "GQ")_ that she and Kanye picked the name North after it was recommended by [Pharrell Williams](/wiki/Pharrell_Williams "Pharrell Williams") and [Anna Wintour](/wiki/Anna_Wintour "Anna Wintour").[\[15\]](#cite_note-Lusk-2014-15) In January 2020, she used a video uploaded to Kylie's [YouTube](/wiki/YouTube "YouTube") account to state that the name North grew on her after [Jay Leno](/wiki/Jay_Leno "Jay Leno") jokingly suggested it while she was appearing on [his talk show](/wiki/The_Tonight_Show_with_Jay_Leno "The Tonight Show with Jay Leno").[\[16\]](#cite_note-16)

West was baptised in the [Armenian Apostolic Church](/wiki/Armenian_Apostolic_Church "Armenian Apostolic Church") at the [Cathedral of Saint James](/wiki/Cathedral_of_Saint_James,_Jerusalem "Cathedral of Saint James, Jerusalem") in [Jerusalem](/wiki/Jerusalem "Jerusalem") in April 2015 during a tour of the [Middle East](/wiki/Middle_East "Middle East"),[\[17\]](#cite_note-17) and attended [Sierra Canyon School](/wiki/Sierra_Canyon_School "Sierra Canyon School"), which had previously been attended by Kendall and Kylie.[\[18\]](#cite_note-18) Growing up, she was involved in a number of her parents' ventures. In January 2015, she appeared in the music video for Kanye's "Only One".[\[19\]](#cite_note-Only_One-19) In April 2016, Kardashian used an episode of her sister's chat show _[Kocktails with Khloé](/wiki/Kocktails_with_Khlo%C3%A9 "Kocktails with Khloé")_ to note that North had flushed an [iPhone](/wiki/IPhone "IPhone") containing an early draft of Kanye's album _[The Life of Pablo](/wiki/The_Life_of_Pablo "The Life of Pablo")_ down the toilet, leading Kanye to have to re-record it from scratch.[\[20\]](#cite_note-20)

She made appearances on her family's program _Keeping Up with the Kardashians_.[\[21\]](#cite_note-21) Aged five, she appeared on the cover of _[Women's Wear Daily](/wiki/Women%27s_Wear_Daily "Women's Wear Daily")_'s annual Beauty Inc. issue.[\[22\]](#cite_note-22) In March 2023, Kim applied for several trademarks in North's name.[\[23\]](#cite_note-23) In September 2023,[\[24\]](#cite_note-24) North, Saint, and Kim voiced Mini, Meteor Max, and Delores in _[Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie](/wiki/Paw_Patrol:_The_Mighty_Movie "Paw Patrol: The Mighty Movie")_.[\[25\]](#cite_note-Paw_Patrol_Atlanta-25) In October 2023, by which time she had accompanied her mother to multiple events in Los Angeles and abroad, she gave a solo interview to _[i-D](/wiki/I-D "I-D")_, in which she expressed several of her hopes and dreams.[\[26\]](#cite_note-26)

### 2024: _Vultures collaborations_ and _The Lion King_ performance

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=North_West_\(musician\)&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: 2024: Vultures collaborations and The Lion King performance")\]

By February 2024, a [TikTok](/wiki/TikTok "TikTok") account North shared with her mother had accrued 18.3 million followers.[\[27\]](#cite_note-27) That month, Kanye West released a video for "[Talking / Once Again](/wiki/Talking_/_Once_Again "Talking / Once Again")", a [single](/wiki/Single_\(music\) "Single (music)") by [¥$](/wiki/%C2%A5$ "¥$"), a supergroup comprising himself and [Ty Dolla Sign](/wiki/Ty_Dolla_Sign "Ty Dolla Sign"), which included a guest verse from North;[\[28\]](#cite_note-28) upon release later that month as part of the group's album _[Vultures 1](/wiki/Vultures_1 "Vultures 1")_, North's contribution was noted by _[NME](/wiki/NME "NME")_ as a rare highlight from an otherwise relentlessly misogynistic album.[\[29\]](#cite_note-29) Later that month, the song peaked at number 30 on the [_Billboard_ Hot 100](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100"),[\[30\]](#cite_note-30) and she performed it at [Accor Arena](/wiki/Accor_Arena "Accor Arena").[\[31\]](#cite_note-Jones-2024-31)

On March 10, West announced her debut album _Elementary School Dropout_, at a performance in [Arizona](/wiki/Arizona "Arizona") plugging ¥$'s second album _[Vultures 2](/wiki/Vultures_2 "Vultures 2")_;[\[31\]](#cite_note-Jones-2024-31) the title referenced Kanye's 2004 album _[The College Dropout](/wiki/The_College_Dropout "The College Dropout")_.[\[32\]](#cite_note-32) She then gave an interview to the then-thirteen-year-old Jazlyn of [Jazzy's World TV](/wiki/Jazzy%27s_World_TV "Jazzy's World TV") at [Rolling Loud](/wiki/Rolling_Loud "Rolling Loud").[\[31\]](#cite_note-Jones-2024-31) In April 2024, ¥$ uploaded a second music video for "Talking", which had been co-directed and written by North, and featured scenes of her with Kanye and with a group of people her own age.[\[33\]](#cite_note-Talking_Teen_Vogue-33)

> "I already know what's coming, you know, that she's not [Whitney Houston](/wiki/Whitney_Houston "Whitney Houston") — duh! Oh, she got the job cause of her parents. North is the moment. They want to see North West on a TikTok, on this, on anything, because she's a personality, a performer, and if anyone wants to hate on a child that is having the time of their lives, fuck you."

— Kim Kardashian just before North's performance[\[34\]](#cite_note-Fuck_1-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-Fuck_2-35)

In May 2024, it was announced that she would perform at the [Hollywood Bowl](/wiki/Hollywood_Bowl "Hollywood Bowl")'s _[The Lion King](/wiki/The_Lion_King "The Lion King") 30th Anniversary – A Live-to-Film Concert Event_ later that month. _[Deadline Hollywood](/wiki/Deadline_Hollywood "Deadline Hollywood")_ drew parallels with the then-recent announcement that [Blue Ivy Carter](/wiki/Blue_Ivy_Carter "Blue Ivy Carter"), a daughter of [Beyoncé](/wiki/Beyonc%C3%A9 "Beyoncé") and [Jay-Z](/wiki/Jay-Z "Jay-Z"), had been hired for a role in _[Mufasa: The Lion King](/wiki/Mufasa:_The_Lion_King "Mufasa: The Lion King")_.[\[36\]](#cite_note-36) For her performance of "[I Just Can't Wait to Be King](/wiki/I_Just_Can%27t_Wait_to_Be_King "I Just Can't Wait to Be King")",[\[37\]](#cite_note-37) West was outfitted by ERL Clothing, who put her in a yellow furry hooded sweatshirt with matching shorts, socks and furry slippers.[\[38\]](#cite_note-38) Her performance was praised by [Jason Weaver](/wiki/Jason_Weaver "Jason Weaver"),[\[39\]](#cite_note-39) who provided the singing voice for that film's cub [Simba](/wiki/Simba "Simba");[\[40\]](#cite_note-40) however, some social media commentators felt that West had only been hired due to her parents' fame.[\[41\]](#cite_note-41) Her role was later defended by Kim on an episode of _[The Kardashians](/wiki/The_Kardashians "The Kardashians")_.[\[34\]](#cite_note-Fuck_1-34)[\[35\]](#cite_note-Fuck_2-35) In August 2024, North and her sister Chicago were featured on the track "Bomb" from ¥$'s album _[Vultures 2](/wiki/Vultures_2 "Vultures 2")_, in which North rapped in [Japanese](/wiki/Japanese_language "Japanese language").[\[42\]](#cite_note-42) That October, she was interviewed by [_Interview_](/wiki/Interview_\(magazine\) "Interview (magazine)"), where she discussed Christianity and Japan.[\[43\]](#cite_note-43)

### 2025–present: Collaborations and _N0rth4evr_

\[[edit](/w/index.php?title=North_West_\(musician\)&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: 2025–present: Collaborations and N0rth4evr")\]

West contributed a rap in Japanese to "Childlike Things" from [FKA Twigs](/wiki/FKA_Twigs "FKA Twigs")'s January 2025 album _[Eusexua](/wiki/Eusexua "Eusexua")_.[\[44\]](#cite_note-44) In a March 2025 video uploaded to [Instagram](/wiki/Instagram "Instagram"), Twigs stated that she was inspired to include a child on the track as it used lyrics she had written when she was 12 or 13 and that she was specifically inspired to feature West after being struck by the confidence she exuded during an interview, having herself been very shy at that age.[\[45\]](#cite_note-45) She also released a video for the track that month.[\[46\]](#cite_note-46)

In March 2025, she featured on "[Lonely Roads Still Go to Sunshine](/wiki/Lonely_Roads_Still_Go_to_Sunshine "Lonely Roads Still Go to Sunshine")", a track Kanye uploaded to [Twitter](/wiki/Twitter "Twitter") that featured Jasmine Williams, [King Combs](/wiki/King_Combs "King Combs"), and the latter's father [Sean Combs](/wiki/Sean_Combs "Sean Combs");[\[47\]](#cite_note-47) the involvement of the last of these prompted Justin Curto of [_Vulture_](/wiki/Vulture_\(website\) "Vulture (website)") to describe the track as "one of the most problematic songs you could imagine", as Diddy had been imprisoned on federal sex-crime charges.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Curto-2025-48) [Caitlin Moran](/wiki/Caitlin_Moran "Caitlin Moran") of _[The Times](/wiki/The_Times "The Times")_ described the collaboration as "in no way a useful career step for her" and criticised Kanye for using it to "continue his demented psychological warfare against his ex-wife — at the expense of their child".[\[49\]](#cite_note-49) Prior to release, Kanye shared screenshots he claimed were between himself and Kim, which claimed that she had requested that North's trademark be signed over to her so she could block North's participation "to protect her";[\[50\]](#cite_note-50) he later deleted both posts.[\[48\]](#cite_note-Curto-2025-48) [Playboi Carti](/wiki/Playboi_Carti "Playboi Carti") subsequently expressed interest in working with North[\[51\]](#cite_note-51) and "Lonely Roads Still Go to Sunshine" later featured on King's extended play (EP), _[Never Stop](/wiki/Never_Stop_\(EP\) "Never Stop (EP)")_ under the shortened title "Lonely Roads".[\[52\]](#cite_note-52)

West would preview her first solo single at Kanye West's Mexico City performance on January 30, 2026, titled "Piercing on My Hand" under the label [Gamma](/wiki/Gamma_\(media_company\) "Gamma (media company)"), who had also signed Kanye in time for his upcoming album _[Bully](/wiki/Bully_\(album\) "Bully (album)")_.[\[2\]](#cite_note-POOL-2) The track would later appear on streaming on February 5 that same year. West released her debut EP, _N0rth4evr_ on May 1, 2026, through Gamma.[\[53\]](#cite_note-53)
